solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Show presented by stripper for man celebrating

indicators.note: the letters are on show, offered up by the run of words stripper for man celebrating, read straight through

explanation.surface: A striptease act laid on for a man marking a special occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presented by' signals that the letters sit inside the final words, from the end of 'stripper' to the start of 'celebrating'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a show put on for an audience is a staged act or turn.

clue.text: Sanction seeing birch raised over student's bottom

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits over, above, the next
in a down clue, raising the word for the birch means writing it upwards, backwards

parts.note: a birch is a rod for corporal punishment, a cane

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Approving corporal punishment for a pupil, a school-discipline image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns CANE upward to ENAC; 'bottom' takes the last letter of 'student's', T.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction a law is to pass it formally into force, a synonym in the legislative sense.

clue.text: More exotic groupie, occasionally active redhead

parts.note: a groupie is a devoted follower, a fan

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of active is taken

parts.note: the head of the word red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A rock fan with fiery hair who is sometimes energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of 'active', CIE; 'redhead' is read as the head of 'red'.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of the adjective meaning elaborate or showy, so more elaborate or exotic.

clue.text: Place elsewhere to speak to the audience

indicators.note: said to the listeners, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to recite is to speak lines from memory

explanation.surface: An instruction to move somewhere and address the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the audience' means the word for 'speak', RECITE, is heard; the hyphenated entry sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To relocate something is to set it at a new site, the prefix meaning again.

clue.text: 'Champion' saddled evenly carrying very old guy

indicators.note: the letters picked out hold the rest inside them, as one carries a load
evenly means the even-numbered letters, second, fourth and sixth, are kept

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for a man, a guy

explanation.surface: A horse saddled for racing bearing an ancient rider named Champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' picks the second, fourth and sixth letters; 'carrying' wraps them round the rest. CAT is old jazz slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to champion a cause is to argue for it, to speak up in support.

clue.text: Surprised expression over droop on sweetheart's bodice

indicators.note: in a down entry this piece sits over the next
in a down entry, on means placed above what follows

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
to sag is to droop
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A gasp at a sagging bodice worn by someone's darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the middle letter E of 'sweet'. COR is a British exclamation like 'gosh'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bodice of a dress is its upper part; the older sense of the word is exactly that garment section.

clue.text: Softening blow for Bond, cradling hero's head

parts.note: a rap is a sharp blow
pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: the word for bond holds the next letter inside it as arms cradle a child

parts.note: cement bonds things together

indicators.note: a head is the first letter of a word

explanation.surface: A punch thrown at James Bond while someone holds a hero's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cradling' puts H, the first letter of 'hero's', inside CEMENT, giving CHEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic thaw: re-establishing friendly relations is a softening of hostility.

clue.text: Fighting odds of mail worker fired for collecting

indicators.note: the first pieces gather the next one in among themselves
the odd-numbered letters, first and third, are taken from the word mail

parts.note: a worker is a kind of ant, a crossword staple
lit means set alight, fired

explanation.surface: A postal worker sacked for collecting mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds of' keeps the first and third letters of 'mail'; 'collecting' means the word for 'fired' sits between those and the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Militant means combative, engaged in fighting, as in a militant group.

clue.text: Almost without turning, beauty's fit and perfect

indicators.note: turning means the trimmed word is read backwards
almost all of the word is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: minus means without
a peach is a beauty, someone very attractive
able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: A near-faultless beauty who is fit and perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts MINUS to MINU, and 'turning' gives UNIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond reproach, so flawless or perfect; impeachment is accusation.

clue.text: Fashionable cooker's fashionable once more

parts.note: an Aga is a range cooker that is something of a status symbol in British country kitchens
in means fashionable, in vogue

explanation.surface: A trendy stove is said to be trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a cast-iron British range cooker, prized in country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: once more means another time, afresh.

clue.text: Coin, surplus say, including one put in tin

indicators.note: the following letters are put inside the symbol for tin

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
over means surplus, left over

indicators.note: the abbreviation takes the next letter within it

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Spare coins, perhaps one dropped into a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers: 'including' puts the numeral inside 'say', and 'put in' sets everything inside the chemical symbol for tin.
explanation.definitionFit: An old British gold coin worth a pound is called by this name.

clue.text: Loyal and ready insurgence with endless murder

parts.note: pat means ready, prepared, as in 'off pat'
a riot is an insurgence, an uprising

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to ice is slang for to murder

explanation.surface: Rebels who are loyal and ready for revolt and killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts ICE, slang for kill, to IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal to one's country is the sense: devoted to the nation.

clue.text: Saw cut down chopper getting TT place

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, losing its last letter

parts.note: an axe is a chopper
the TT motorcycle races are held on the Isle of Man, abbreviated IOM

explanation.surface: A saw and a felled tree beside a chopper heading for the TT races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the tool but is a saying. The Isle of Man hosts the TT motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, a self-evident truth.

clue.text: Limos perhaps following very big ceremony

indicators.note: the vehicles come after the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
limos are examples of cars

explanation.surface: Stretch limos lined up after a grand awards ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Awards are a ceremony named after their statuettes.

clue.text: At last, the right men for the job?

definitions.text: At last, the right men for the job?

parts.words: At last, the right men for the job?
parts.note: shoemakers work on a last, the foot-shaped form, so they are the ones for a job on a last

explanation.surface: A relieved cry that the right workers have finally been hired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' means finally, but a last is the shoemaker's foot-shaped block.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoe repairers work with a last, so they suit a job done on one.

clue.text: Period when English Queen's put in cheap accommodation

indicators.note: the letters for English and Queen are placed inside the word for period

parts.note: a stage is a period or phase
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: An era when an English queen was lodged in cheap rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: On a passenger ship this was the cheapest class of travel, lowest-fare berths.

clue.text: Disgust of ocean in half oceanic ocean centre

indicators.note: the word for ocean goes in the shortened word
only the first half of the word for oceanic is used

parts.note: nautical means of the sea, oceanic
the sea is an ocean

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A wordy jumble of oceans that sounds like disgust at the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the first four of eight letters of the word for oceanic; 'centre' takes E from the second 'ocean'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sicken or revolt someone is to disgust them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Ordinary, slightly in drag, having change of heart

indicators.note: the phrase for slightly goes inside the altered word
the two middle letters of the word for drag swap places

parts.note: to haul is to drag
a bit means slightly

explanation.surface: Someone mildly in drag who then has second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having change of heart' turns HAUL into HUAL; A BIT goes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual or customary, so ordinary, as in a habitual route.

clue.text: Swing from section, turning with dexterity in articulation

indicators.note: turning means the word for section is read backwards

parts.note: a part is a section

indicators.note: in articulation means as spoken, so the word is heard

parts.note: ease means dexterity, effortless skill

explanation.surface: A gymnast swinging out of a section, twisting with nimble joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes TRAP from PART; 'in articulation' gives EZE, heard as EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus swing is a bar hung on ropes, used by aerialists.

clue.text: Exercise pressure preceding spasm of digestion

indicators.note: the first letters come before the next word

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
P is the physics symbol for pressure
a tic is a muscular spasm

explanation.surface: Workout strain bringing on a stomach cramp.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to digestion, as in a peptic ulcer of the gut.

clue.text: Old former wife can cheat heartlessly

parts.note: an ex is a former wife
a tin is a can

indicators.note: without its heart, only the outer letters of the word cheat remain

explanation.surface: An ex-wife who can cheat without remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' keeps C and T from 'cheat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Died out, so no longer existing and belonging to the past.

clue.text: Laugh in derision comprehending stunt

indicators.note: comprehending means including, so the phrase holds the letters within itself

explanation.surface: Mocking laughter at someone's daredevil stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunt' looks like a noun, a daredevil act, but it is the verb meaning to hold back growth.
explanation.definitionFit: To stunt growth is to impede or hold it back, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Island providing short holiday with no outside elements

indicators.note: each word loses its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: small means short
a stay is a visit or holiday

explanation.surface: An island offering a brief holiday free of bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no outside elements' strips SMALL to MAL and STAY to TA. The 'elements' look like weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean island nation south of Sicily.

clue.text: Bit of perfect sex takes over missing weekend

indicators.note: over means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: all can mean complete or perfect
it is slang for sex

indicators.note: missing means the end letter of the week is left out

parts.note: nicks means takes, steals
the end of week is its final letter

explanation.surface: A racy line about the briefest of romps over a weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weekend' is the last letter of 'week', which 'missing' removes; 'over' then reads the whole string backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny trace or spark, so the smallest bit of something.

clue.text: A game of chance is million against

parts.note: a lot means a very large number, loosely a million
to means against, touching, as in face to face

explanation.surface: A lottery wins a million against the odds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bingo-like game played with numbered cards and drawn numbers.

clue.text: Ladies trip over to employ single nanny …

indicators.note: to employ means to take on, so the letter goes inside
over means the two words are read backwards

parts.note: dames are ladies
a run is a short trip
I, one, is single

explanation.surface: Ladies tumbling over themselves to hire a lone nanny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DAMES+RUN to NURSEMAD; 'to employ' takes I in.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after children, a nanny.

clue.text: … accompanying birth, bearing a giant almost

parts.note: N, north, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: tall means giant, lofty

explanation.surface: Continuing the nanny story: a birth bearing almost a giant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts TALL to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the time of birth, as in natal day or prenatal care.

clue.text: Party's voting — Conservative's sent to start hugging supporter

indicators.note: the rearranged word holds the next piece inside it
the letter is moved to the beginning of the word

parts.note: an election is voting
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a bra is a supporter

explanation.surface: Election-night party talk: the Tory sent off to hug a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent to start' moves C to the front: CELETION; 'hugging' takes BRA in.
explanation.definitionFit: A party is a celebration, a festive gathering.
